validator: draft 1 passes (no problems, soft or warnings); the faults below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named in one line up front and built on lesson 1's own boat, f(x) = x², and its own chord from 3 s to 4 s (7 m per s), so nothing is retaught.

The brief's picture is followed exactly: P fixed at 3 s, a draggable Q, a slider shrinking the gap, a table settling 7, 6.5, 6.1, 6.01 on 6, a zoom lens, and δy/δx becoming dy/dx as the MCA defines it [5].

Every misconception in the course brief for lesson 2 has a DO screen and is shown failing in explain: 'a limit is never reached' (step 12 option, and 'exactly 6, not nearly 6'), the rate as a formula without meaning (step 11 asks what −20 L per min says), the tangent 'only touches once' (step 8's upright line), and the d's cancelling (step 10, 9 ÷ 3 = 3 against 6).

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), ending with two mixed puzzles (11, 12), each wrong option a named slip: not dividing, y ÷ x, the last chord taken as the rate, the height read as the rate.
Every number is assumed (example rules from lesson 1, the analogy's marks) or computed from f(x) = x² or f(x) = 2(10 − x)²; all chord values checked by hand.
fix: Causal step skipped (fault 1): the draft says the chord slopes settle on 6 but gives Dan nothing he can see that makes 6 exact rather than a guess. The table shows it: in every row the amount above 6 is the gap itself (7 = 6 + 1, 6.5 = 6 + 0.5, 6.1 = 6 + 0.1, 6.01 = 6 + 0.01), so shrinking the gap shrinks the extra towards nothing. Say so, and that the next lesson shows why. Also say why chords ending at 3 s read below 6: the boat was slower before 3 s.

False absolutes (fault 2): 'until you cannot tell it from the tangent' is not literally true at any zoom; say 'until it is hard to tell'. 'textbooks build the tangent exactly this way' generalises one cited text; state the fact with its footnote instead. The brief's 'the chord swings into the tangent' should be 'towards'. Practice's 'read off the number both sides settle on' needs the case where they disagree (a sharp corner: no single rate), or it reads as always.
The upright line's 'no slope at all' skips its reason: along it Δx is 0, so Δy ÷ Δx cannot be worked out. Give the reason in a clause.

Talking about the lesson instead of teaching (fault 7): 'so this lesson puts the rate first and treats the tangent as its picture' is meta. Turn it into the teaching point: the rate is the meaning, the tangent is a picture of it, and one teacher writing for the MAA argues the derivative should not be understood through the tangent's slope [7].

Analogy (recommended shape: from Dan's trade): the car between road marks is the textbook picture. A motor running up to speed, its shaft turns counted over shorter and shorter windows, is from his own work, reproduces the main result (averages over shorter windows settle on the speed at that moment) and has a specific, correct break: a turn count is a whole number, so over a very short window it reads 0 or 1 and the counting error swamps the answer, while the maths has no smallest gap.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with these five fixes; nothing else needs to change.
